method_definition: Apply the improved MeanFlow velocity-regression identity to every causal target token.
Sample an independent interval pair (r_k, t_k) for each target token k.

For token k, differentiate only with respect to its current corrupted value z_k and query time t_k; treat actions, earlier corrupted tokens, their noise levels, and other context as fixed conditioning in that partial JVP.
Decouple each token's iMF query pair (r_k, t_k) from the history exposure times tau_j, while using the same per-token Gaussian draw to form the query and history views.
Train across an explicit mixture of clean-history, independently timed corrupted-history, and clean-prefix/teacher-corrupted-suffix supervision contexts.
Generate each autoregressive world transition at the primary operating point with one network function evaluation.
excluded_claims: reproducing the complete Dreamer 4 agent or its unreleased training system
inventing flow matching, MeanFlow, improved MeanFlow, per-token noise schedules, causal sequence flow, or one-step MeanFlow control

proving that learned scheduled conditionals agree with the data and all-subsequence marginals, provide a tractable likelihood, control rollout error, identify epistemic uncertainty, or prevent planner exploitation
establishing empirical superiority before the frozen confirmatory benchmark is complete

search_boundary.evidence_policy: Primary papers, official proceedings pages, author project pages, and author-maintained code repositories only. Discovery indexes and secondary summaries were not used as claim evidence.
families_checked: flow matching and conditional flow matching
diffusion forcing, rolling diffusion, and variable-history video diffusion
token-wise, autoregressive, streaming, multi-time, and fully causal continuous generation
flow-matching and MeanFlow world models, dynamics models, and control policies
limitations: This is a bounded literature audit, not a patent search or proof that no unpublished, non-indexed, or differently named method exists.
Very recent 2026 preprints may change after the cutoff.
Absence of the exact combination in the audited primary sources supports only careful combination-novelty wording, never a priority claim.

sources.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
sources.relevance: Introduces simulation-free vector-field regression along fixed conditional probability paths; it owns the basic conditional flow-matching ingredient.

sources.title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling
sources.relevance: Introduces interval-average velocity and the MeanFlow identity for from-scratch 1-NFE generation.

sources.title: Improved Mean Flows: On the Challenges of Fastforward Generative Models
sources.relevance: Recasts MeanFlow as instantaneous-velocity regression through an average-velocity network, using a predicted marginal-velocity tangent and boundary evaluation; this owns the iMF objective used by the proposal.

sources.title: One Step Diffusion via Shortcut Models
sources.relevance: Conditions one network on requested step size and constructs larger-step targets from two stopped-gradient half steps, supporting one or several inference steps.

sources.title: Diffusion Forcing: Next-token Prediction Meets Full-Sequence Diffusion
sources.relevance: Trains causal sequence models with independent per-token noise levels, partially noised histories, flexible horizons, and an all-subsequence variational interpretation.

sources.title: Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models
sources.relevance: Combines Diffusion Forcing and Shortcut Models in an action-conditioned block-causal world model, with per-token signal levels and step sizes, x-prediction, a stopped-gradient two-half-step target, context corruption, and K=4 inference per frame.

sources.title: Rolling Diffusion Models
sources.relevance: Assigns progressive frame-dependent corruption across a temporal window and rolls the window forward; heterogeneous time schedules across sequence positions predate this proposal.

sources.title: History-Guided Video Diffusion
sources.relevance: Builds a Diffusion Forcing Transformer that supports flexible amounts of history and long video rollouts, narrowing any claim around mixed clean or corrupted history conditioning.

sources.title: Probabilistic Forecasting via Autoregressive Flow Matching
sources.relevance: FlowTime factorizes a future trajectory into conditional next-observation densities represented by a shared flow, establishing autoregressive flow matching for dynamical forecasting.

sources.title: FELLE: Autoregressive Speech Synthesis with Token-Wise Coarse-to-Fine Flow Matching
sources.relevance: Combines autoregressive continuous-token generation with token-wise flow matching; token-wise causal flow is therefore not itself new.

sources.title: Transition Matching: Scalable and Flexible Generative Modeling
sources.relevance: Introduces autoregressive and full-history transition matching as partially and fully causal continuous-state generation paradigms.

sources.title: Self-Supervised Flow Matching for Scalable Multi-Modal Synthesis
sources.relevance: Self-Flow's dual-timestep schedule applies heterogeneous noise levels across tokens; a multi-time token schedule cannot be claimed as novel here.

sources.title: StreamFlow: Streaming Audio Generation from Discrete Tokens via Streaming Flow Matching
sources.venue_or_status: NeurIPS 2025 proceedings; primary page exposes year rather than publication day
sources.relevance: Uses causal noising and predicts multiple time-indexed vector fields in a token-wise streaming generator, making it especially close to the proposal's multi-time causal sequence structure.

sources.title: Inference Time Policy Optimization for Offline RL with Differentiable World Models
sources.relevance: Uses a one-step MeanFlow sampler in a differentiable world-model pipeline for imagined rollouts, directly precluding a broad claim that this is the first MeanFlow world model.

sources.title: Flow Matching in Feature Space for Stochastic World Modeling
sources.relevance: FlowWM performs stochastic flow matching directly in pretrained feature space and studies temporal consistency and horizon robustness in a world model.

sources.title: Flow-JEPA: Flow Matching for Robust Latent Dynamics in JEPA World Models
sources.relevance: Uses conditional flow matching to jointly generate future latent trajectories from the current observation and actions, precluding a broad trajectory-flow-world-model claim.

sources.title: MP1: MeanFlow Tames Policy Learning in 1-step for Robotic Manipulation
sources.relevance: Applies MeanFlow to 1-NFE action-trajectory generation; it is a policy rather than a world dynamics model, but blocks broad MeanFlow-trajectory novelty wording.

sources.title: Causal-rCM: A Unified Teacher-Forcing and Self-Forcing Open Recipe for Autoregressive Diffusion Distillation in Streaming Video Generation and Interactive World Models
sources.relevance: Its teacher-forcing continuous-time CM/MeanFlow construction explicitly gives clean causal context a zero JVP tangent and moves only the noisy target branch; it also describes noisy historical context with loss only on the current target. This directly establishes broad fixed-context causal-JVP prior art.

sources.title: AlphaFlow: Understanding and Improving MeanFlow Models
sources.relevance: Decomposes MeanFlow into trajectory-flow-matching and trajectory-consistency terms and gives a formulation unifying trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Models, and MeanFlow. Their relationship is not an open novelty claim for this project.

sources.title: SplitMeanFlow: Interval Splitting Consistency in Few-Step Generative Modeling
sources.relevance: Derives interval-splitting consistency for average velocity and proves the MeanFlow differential identity is recovered as the split approaches an endpoint. The differential-versus-splitting relation is prior theory.

sources.title: Autoregressive One-Step Generative Modeling for Dynamical System Forecasting
sources.relevance: MeLISA's Window-Consistency MeanFlow is in the improved-MeanFlow lineage and trains a stochastic autoregressive spatiotemporal transition kernel with 1 NFE per forecast block. It is not the identical iMF objective: its displayed WinC-MF JVP uses the pathwise epsilon-x tangent rather than iMF's predicted marginal-velocity tangent. It uses one shared (r,t) pair across frames and adds a finite-lag Time Increment Consistency loss.

claim_elements.element: Simulation-free regression of a conditional straight-path velocity field
claim_elements.audit_finding: This is the core flow-matching construction.

claim_elements.element: Interval-average velocity identity and direct 1-NFE generation
claim_elements.audit_finding: MeanFlow supplies both the identity and the one-step operating point.

claim_elements.element: Improved MeanFlow v-space regression through an average-velocity predictor, with a predicted marginal-velocity JVP tangent and boundary evaluation
claim_elements.audit_finding: The proposal reuses the published iMF objective rather than deriving a new MeanFlow identity.

claim_elements.element: Independent noise or signal levels across sequence tokens
claim_elements.audit_finding: Per-token or heterogeneous sequence corruption is already central to Diffusion Forcing and related work.

claim_elements.element: Independent iMF interval pairs (r_k, t_k) for causal target tokens
claim_elements.audit_finding: iMF supplies interval pairs; sequence methods supply token-dependent times; Causal-rCM supplies causal continuous-time CM/MeanFlow. Independently sampled per-target iMF pairs decoupled from history exposure times were not found verbatim in the audited sources.
claim_elements.residual_claim: A narrow schedule/objective combination whose value must be established theoretically or empirically.

claim_elements.element: Fixed-context partial JVP: differentiate token k only through (z_k, t_k), holding actions and all realized causal-history values and times fixed
claim_elements.audit_finding: Holding conditions fixed is standard conditional differentiation, and Causal-rCM Equation (17) explicitly assigns the clean causal context a zero tangent while moving only the noisy target branch.
claim_elements.residual_claim: Correctness-critical implementation semantics, not a priority-bearing novelty.

claim_elements.element: Mixture of clean-history, corrupted-history, and teacher-corrupted-suffix supervision contexts
claim_elements.audit_finding: Flexible clean or corrupted history and causal rolling/suffix patterns are prior art. Causal-rCM also explicitly replaces clean history by noisy history while supervising the current target. The exact three-way mixture with independent history times and a shared-noise two-view coupling is implementation-specific.
claim_elements.residual_claim: A narrow schedule-mixture and coupling ablation, not a standalone foundational contribution.

claim_elements.element: Causal, action-conditioned continuous-token world modeling and imagination rollouts
claim_elements.audit_finding: Causal sequence diffusion/flow and action-conditioned flow world models already exist.
claim_elements.residual_claim: None at this level of abstraction.

claim_elements.element: Requested-step conditioning with stopped-gradient two-half-step shortcut targets
claim_elements.audit_finding: This is the shortcut baseline, not part of the claimed iMF contribution.

claim_elements.element: A one-step MeanFlow sampler used as a world-model transition for control
claim_elements.audit_finding: ITPO explicitly studies a one-step MeanFlow sampler in a differentiable world-model rollout pipeline, while MeLISA supplies a 1-NFE stochastic autoregressive dynamical transition kernel.
claim_elements.residual_claim: The proposed method may differ in per-token iMF scheduling and action-control scope, but cannot claim the broad category.

claim_elements.element: Flow matching that jointly predicts an action-conditioned future latent trajectory
claim_elements.audit_finding: Flow-JEPA directly occupies this broad design space; FlowWM further establishes stochastic flow world modeling.
claim_elements.residual_claim: Only objective- and conditioning-level distinctions remain.

claim_elements.element: The full trajectory-iMF combination: independent per-target iMF intervals decoupled from history exposure times, shared-noise query/history views, the three-way schedule mixture, action conditioning, and 1-NFE autoregressive transitions
claim_elements.audit_finding: No exact combination was found in the audited primary sources through the cutoff. Causal-rCM already has teacher-forced causal continuous-time CM/MeanFlow with a zero context tangent and noisy-context extension. MeLISA is the closest 1-NFE autoregressive-dynamics precedent in the improved-MeanFlow lineage, but its displayed JVP uses the pathwise epsilon-x tangent instead of iMF's predicted marginal velocity and it shares one (r,t) pair across its temporal window.
claim_elements.residual_claim: At most an apparently unreported narrow combination of decoupled per-token query/history schedules, shared-noise two-view construction, and schedule mixing; this is not a priority claim.

claim_elements.element: Trajectory iMF outperforms faithful Dreamer-4-style shortcut forcing under matched budgets
claim_elements.audit_finding: Neither paper tests this comparison, and local smoke results cannot establish it.
claim_elements.residual_claim: Requires the frozen paired confirmatory benchmark on both rollout fidelity and actor return.

claim_elements.element: Agreement of learned scheduled conditionals with data and all-subsequence marginals, tractable likelihood interpretation, and a bound on environment-time rollout error
claim_elements.audit_finding: Measurable normalized autoregressive conditional kernels already induce a normalized joint rollout law by sequential composition. Diffusion Forcing additionally provides an all-subsequence variational result, and MeLISA adds explicit finite-lag temporal-increment consistency, but the proposed trajectory-iMF objective has no proof that its scheduled conditionals agree with data or all-subsequence marginals, no tractable likelihood result, and no control-error bound.

claim_elements.element: Epistemic uncertainty, calibration under distribution shift, and protection against planner or actor exploitation
claim_elements.audit_finding: The Gaussian source models aleatoric randomness. It does not by itself identify epistemic uncertainty or constrain optimized policies to trustworthy regions.
claim_elements.residual_claim: Requires explicit ensembles or posterior approximations, calibration tests, and policy-exploitation diagnostics.

claim_elements.element: MeanFlow generation of a continuous trajectory for control
claim_elements.audit_finding: MP1 generates action trajectories with MeanFlow in one NFE; it is not a dynamics model, but narrows trajectory-level wording.
claim_elements.residual_claim: The world-dynamics role and fixed-context iMF formulation remain distinguishing details.

claim_elements.element: A unifying relation among trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Models, and MeanFlow
claim_elements.audit_finding: AlphaFlow explicitly decomposes MeanFlow and places trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Models, and MeanFlow in one objective family.
claim_elements.residual_claim: None; the benchmark may compare members of this family but must not claim to discover the relation.

claim_elements.element: MeanFlow's differential identity as the infinitesimal limit of interval-splitting consistency
claim_elements.audit_finding: SplitMeanFlow derives the algebraic interval-splitting identity and proves the differential MeanFlow identity is recovered at the infinitesimal endpoint limit.
claim_elements.residual_claim: None; any new theorem must go beyond this relationship and address causal conditional trajectories.

claim_elements.element: MeanFlow/iMF-style training of a stochastic 1-NFE autoregressive dynamical transition kernel over temporal windows
claim_elements.audit_finding: MeLISA's Window-Consistency MeanFlow is the closest one-evaluation autoregressive dynamical-forecasting precedent in the improved-MeanFlow lineage. Its displayed JVP uses the pathwise epsilon-x tangent, rather than the predicted marginal-velocity tangent of the iMF objective proposed here.
claim_elements.residual_claim: The exact iMF objective, independent per-token query intervals, separately timed corrupted causal histories, shared-noise two-view coupling, and action-conditioned control remain narrower differences.

verdict.summary: No exact combination was found in the audited primary literature through 2026-09-10, but all major ingredients have close prior art. Causal-rCM already establishes a fixed-context causal JVP construction for continuous-time consistency/MeanFlow training, including a noisy-context extension. MeLISA is the closest stochastic 1-NFE autoregressive-dynamics precedent in the improved-MeanFlow lineage and uses a shared interval across its temporal window, but its displayed JVP uses the pathwise epsilon-x tangent rather than iMF's predicted marginal velocity. AlphaFlow already unifies trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Models, and MeanFlow, while SplitMeanFlow establishes the interval-splitting/differential-limit relation. The defensible residual is only an apparently unreported narrow combination of iMF with independent per-target query intervals decoupled from history exposure times, shared-noise query/history views, and a three-way schedule mixture—not a new foundational identity and not a priority claim.
allowed_wording: We study an iMF objective with decoupled per-token query and history-exposure schedules for causal world-model transitions.

Among the primary sources audited through 2026-09-10, we did not find the exact combination of independent token-wise iMF intervals, separately sampled history exposure times, shared-noise query/history views, a three-way causal schedule mixture, and 1-NFE autoregressive world transitions.

The contribution is a narrow method combination and controlled empirical test; fixed-context causal JVPs themselves are prior art in Causal-rCM, MeLISA is the closest MeanFlow/iMF-style 1-NFE autoregressive-dynamics precedent but does not use the identical iMF tangent, and the remaining ingredients derive from iMF, Diffusion Forcing, causal sequence flow, and prior flow world models.
prohibited_wording: the first flow-matching trajectory world model
the first per-token or multi-time flow model
the first fixed-context causal JVP for MeanFlow
a new unification of trajectory flow matching, Shortcut Models, and MeanFlow
a new proof that MeanFlow is an infinitesimal interval-splitting limit
the first improved-MeanFlow autoregressive dynamical world model
evidence_required_before_strengthening: A completed confirmatory paired benchmark satisfying the frozen superiority rule.
A broader camera-ready literature update and citation chaining immediately before submission.
Formal results showing agreement of scheduled conditionals with data/all-subsequence marginals, a tractable likelihood interpretation, or controlled rollout error if such theorem claims are made.
